statement.text:
(a) $($ Meridional Rank Conjecture $)$ Is the meridional $\operatorname{rank} \mu(L)$ of every link
$L$ equal to its bridge number $b(L)$?
(b) Given two knots $K_{1}, K_{2} \subset S^{3}$ such that $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{1})$ and $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{2})$ have
the same finite quotients, does $\mu(K_{1}) = \mu(K_{2})$? In particular, is it possible
to explicitly detect the meridional $\operatorname{rank} \mu(K)$ of a knot $K \subset S^{3}$ from the
finite quotients of $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K)$?
(c) Given two links $L_{1}, L_{2} \subset S^{3}$, if there exists a surjective homomorphism
$\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus L_{1}) \twoheadrightarrow\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus L_{2})$ that sends the meridians of $L_{1}$ to the meridians
of $L_{2}$, do the bridge numbers satisfy $b(L_{1}) \geq b(L_{2})$?
(d) Given two knots $K_{1}, K_{2} \subset S^{3}$, if there exists a surjective homomorphism
$\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{1}) \twoheadrightarrow\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K_{2})$ (which may not send meridians to meridians):
(i) Do the meridional ranks satisfy $\mu(K_{1}) \geq \mu(K_{2})$?
(ii) Do the bridge numbers satisfy $b(K_{1}) \geq b(K_{2})$?
(e) Let $K \subset S^{3}$ be a hyperbolic knot. Is every subgroup of $\pi_{1}(S^{3}\setminus K)$ generated
by at most $b(K) - 1$ meridians free? See [BJW18].
